lead: Clearwater plumbing deals with storm surge, salt air, slab homes and aging cast-iron drains. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Clearwater.
risk: cast-iron drain failures, storm-surge damage and slab leaks
risk_short: old drains, storm surge and slab leaks
why: Harbor Oaks, Skycrest and much of central Clearwater have homes from the 1920s to the 1970s with cast-iron drains under the slab. Countryside was built mostly in the 1970s and 1980s.
Hurricanes Helene and Milton in 2024 sent surge into Clearwater Beach and low areas. Salt air corrodes outdoor fittings and water heater parts.
water: Clearwater treats groundwater with reverse osmosis and buys some water from Pinellas County Utilities. It is moderately hard.
tips: Have cast-iron drains scoped in older homes.
Shut off the main valve before a hurricane evacuation.
Have the water heater checked after any flood.
Rinse and check outdoor fittings for corrosion.
areas: PipeMend works Downtown and in Clearwater Beach, Countryside, Island Estates, Morningside, Skycrest, Harbor Oaks and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Clearwater Planning and Development Department, and plumbing contractors are licensed by the Florida Construction Industry Licensing Board.

faq.q: What should Clearwater homes check after storm surge?
faq.a: Have the water heater, gas lines and sewer line checked before regular use. Salt water ruins heater controls and silt clogs drains. Keep photos for insurance.
